items.title: the walk's debug-profile stack frame grew past the seal's 25% margin at M110 S6 (the id windows, next @f99dc28e): `deep_nesting::a_thirty_level_chain_still_fits_libtests_own_two_mib_thread` overflows the 1.5 MiB canary thread, fits 1664 KiB, and still fits libtest's 2 MiB - the margin is 20%, down from over 25% at v0.47.0
items.discussion: the Order 50 seal (seal-68f25eb1.out: `canary@1.5MiB exit=100`; canary-bisect.log: green at 5fe24f86, 33444b25, 2b3fdf9d, 549dc109, 7b0c238f; red from f99dc28e on); M110 S6 (incr-50 C2: `walk_module_items`, the per-item windows, the per-constraint anchor); Order 44 (the walk's frame grew past 2 MiB and only Windows CI saw it - the canary's reason); seal.sh's canary leg (`VILAN_CANARY_STACK_KIB=1536`, dev profile)
items.body: The bisect over the order's merge points puts the growth at the C2 merge (M110 S6): each level of the module walk now carries the window bookkeeping (the anchor, the lane cursors, the demand record) in its own frame at opt-level 0, and the 30-level method chain (`"seed".trim().trim()...`) that fit 1.5 MiB at v0.47.0 needs between 1536 and 1664 KiB now. At the real 2 MiB thread all 18 pins pass; CI's ci-test leg (opt-level 1) is green; nothing a user runs is affected (release builds have far smaller frames). Door: hoist the per-level window state out of the recursive frame (one struct on the walker, written once per item, not per level), or box the rarely-used census fields; the measure is the canary at 1536 back to green with the per-level frame size printed once under VILAN_COUNTERS. Did NOT hold the v0.48.0 cut (the canary is a seal-only margin probe; the cut gates CI + the perf verdict); the owner may rule otherwise. Pin: the existing canary leg. Sizing S; incr-50's ground (Order 51, with S7).
